events.message: Collecting evidence from the repo and deck
Found 6,089 source lines, 5 test cases and 40 commits
Read 2 docs and 0 decks, opened 0 demo pages and described 0 screenshots
The judge is writing the council review

review.task_fit: yes: it is a working day-to-day resident tool that cuts landfill waste by rescuing items left at trash sheds, which sits on the quality-of-life side of the Smart City theme, but with no municipal data or city-service integration the fit is partial rather than strong.

scores.why: A real urban habit (posts about trash-shed finds scrolling away) is served by a working pipeline where vision captioning feeds embeddings and a calibrated reranker with measured thresholds. The free-exchange concept itself is not new, so the novelty is in the matching, not the idea.

Waste reduction is a genuine resident pain, but the evidence confirms there is no municipal data feed, no city-staff role and no mobility, energy or crisis dimension anywhere in the code. The smart-city link rests on quality-of-life framing alone, which supports the middle reading over both the strict no-fit and the strong-fit view.

The end-to-end flow works (post, semantic search, photo upload, notifications), browsing needs no login, and the README ships an APK, seed data and a one-command start. Alerts require login, the free tier allows one watch filter, OTP is a fixed mock, and notifications only arrive by polling.

The Flutter theme code is coherent (Material 3 palette, Rubik typography, styled navigation), but no deck was provided and 0 of 42 screenshots were described, so visual quality cannot be verified from the evidence.

About 6,100 lines across a real FastAPI backend with pgvector, migrations, S3 storage, EXIF stripping, JWT auth and reranker matching, plus a Flutter client, in 40 event commits. This is offset by only 5 test cases, no vector or geospatial indexes, and synchronous AI calls in request handlers.

review.live_demo: none found in the form or README
review.built_during_event: yes: 40 commits by 2 authors, 2026-10-03 15:57 to 2026-10-05 12:54 UTC
strengths: Real, measured AI pipeline: Jina embeddings and reranker, Gemini vision captioning and query expansion wired into the listing and filter paths, with documented thresholds.
Privacy engineering beyond the demo norm: EXIF stripped by re-encoding and public coordinates rounded to about 100 m.
Honest internal docs (stan-obecny.md) that separate the target spec from what actually works.
Practical demo path: release APK, seeded Warsaw listings and a one-command start script.
weaknesses: No municipal or urban data source and no city-staff role anywhere in the code, so the smart-city case rests on framing and the platform depends entirely on its own user-generated listings, a two-sided cold start.
The core alert promise is weak at scale: notifications are poll-only with no push, and OTP is a hardcoded 123456 mock with no real SMS gateway.
Missed deliverables: no presentation deck and a submission form left essentially unfilled, so with 0 of 42 screenshots described the UI cannot be judged and the README is the only pitch.
Sparse tests (5 cases), no PostGIS, Redis or Celery, and no integration with the real Facebook group posts the project itself names as the problem.
red_flags: One commit landed after the deadline (1 of 40; the other 39 were during the event, so this is minor).
No demo check in the evidence pack verified the README's hosted-backend and APK claims.
review.verdict: A genuinely engineered and honestly documented zero-waste resident tool with real semantic matching and privacy care, whose smart-city claim rests on quality-of-life framing alone, with no urban data integration, poll-only alerts, a mocked OTP and a missing deck and submission form.
